# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Switch WAF rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (priority 1) in WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 from Action=Count{} to Action=Block{} — DECISION POINT: confirm intent first, as the dominant source is an Artillery load test, not confirmed-malicious traffic.

## Reasoning
During 2026-10-10 18:00–18:15 UTC the WebACL detected a single-source flood from 198.51.100.10 (33,609 reqs, 96.1%) — the rate-based rule matched 34,067 times — but blocked nothing because its Action is Count (monitor-only). Net: 34,972 ALLOW / 2 BLOCK. Setting the rule to Block closes the enforcement gap. The change is fully reversible (revert Action to Count). CAVEAT: blocking will interrupt the Artillery load test; operator must confirm intent, or prefer a scoped IPSet exemption for approved load-test IPs. Alternatives: scoped IPSet block of 198.51.100.10, or raise the 300/300s threshold if too aggressive for legitimate bursts.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Single-source request flood on CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001
**Description:** During 2026-10-10 18:00:00–18:15:00 UTC a single client IP 198.51.100.10 (US) generated 33,609 of 34,974 WAF request records (96.1%) against distribution EEXAMPLE000001 (d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net), using the Artillery load-testing tool and exercising the e-commerce funnel (/cart, /catalog, /home, /checkout, /checkout/payment, /checkout/delivery). It far exceeded the per-IP rate limit of 300 req/300s but was not throttled. A minor unrelated sidecar of vulnerability scanning came from 198.51.100.20.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T18:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Single IP 198.51.100.10 drove 96% of traffic, all allowed
**Description:** Athena over waf_logs (full-window, exact): action breakdown 34,972 ALLOW / 2 BLOCK / 34,974 total. Per-IP: 198.51.100.10 = 33,609 reqs (ALLOW, all 33,609 matched the rate rule in COUNT); 198.51.100.30 = 1,351 reqs (ALLOW, 458 rate-matched); 198.51.100.20 = 14 reqs (12 ALLOW, 2 BLOCK). COUNT never appears as a terminating action — matches land in nonTerminatingMatchingRules while the request stays ALLOW.
**Cascades to:** symptom-abusive-traffic

### Root Cause: Rate-based rule in Count mode (CloudFront default) — flood detected but never blocked
**Description:** AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (Priority 1, Limit 300 req/IP per 300s) has Action=Count, the default for CloudFront-created WebACLs (CreatedByCloudFront-*). It matched over-limit requests 34,067 times in COUNT (non-terminating) mode in the window — including all 33,609 of 198.51.100.10's requests — yet allowed every one. This is the fundamental cause the flood went unthrottled; switching the rule to Block (and/or scoping an IP block / tuning the threshold) is what would stop recurrence. The counting was continuous across 17:00–18:30, so this is a steady configuration state, not a change at 18:00.
**Cascades to:** cause-single-source, symptom-abusive-traffic

## Other Gaps

### get_sampled_requests unavailable for historical window
**Description:** The WAF get_sampled_requests API only accepts time windows within the last 3 hours; the incident is ~5 days old, so that fallback was unusable. Direct get_object and S3 Select were also impractical (each log object decompresses to ~1.5M tokens; S3 Select returned MethodNotAllowed). Analysis relied on server-side Athena aggregation over the waf_logs table — fully worked around, no residual blocker.
